items.readable_text:
Content:
Whenever you move a digit one space to the left in a place value chart, the value of the digit becomes ten times larger.

Content:
Let's use this idea to compare the size of the digit [MATH: 3] in the following two numbers:

Content:
[MATH: {\color{blue}3}8, \qquad 97{\color{red}3}]

Content:
We can compare the relative sizes of the digit [MATH: 3] for each number using a place value chart:

Content:
- First, we write down the place value chart for [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}8{:}]

| hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{lightgray}{0}] | [MATH: \color{blue}3] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}{8}] |
- Then, we write down the place value chart for [MATH: 97{\color{red}{3}}{:}]

| hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{lightgray}{9}] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}{7}] | [MATH: \color{red}3] |
- To compare the sizes of the two digits, we need to move one place to the left.

| hundreds | tens | ones |
| | [MATH: \color{blue}3] | [MATH: \color{red}3] |
| [IMG: /graphics/0257b37fd0a9e1ec6b1cbd4031a533d0] |

Content:
Since the digit [MATH: \color{blue}3] in [MATH: {\color{blue}3}8] is once space to the left of the digit [MATH: \color{red}3] in [MATH: 97{\color{red}3},] we can make the following conclusion:

Content:
> The value of the digit [MATH: \color{blue}3] in [MATH: {\color{blue}3}8] is [MATH: 10] times larger than the value of the digit [MATH: \color{red}3] in [MATH: 97{\color{red}3}.]

Content:
- First, we write down the place value chart for [MATH: 4,{\color{blue}2}11{:}]

| thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{lightgray}4] | [MATH: \color{blue}2] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}1] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}1] |

| thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{lightgray}{0}] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}{0}] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}1] | [MATH: \color{red}2] |
- To compare the sizes of the two digits, we need to move two places to the left:

| thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| | [MATH: \color{blue}2] | | [MATH: \color{red}2] |
| [IMG: /graphics/fca337b2cbbe679601303cc24abce6f0] |

Content:
Now, note the following:

Content:
- Whenever you move a digit one space to the left, the value of the digit becomes [MATH: 10] times larger.
- So, whenever you move a digit two spaces to the left, the value of the digit becomes [MATH: 10\times 10 = 100] times larger!

Content:
Therefore, we can make the following conclusion:

Content:
> The value of the digit [MATH: \color{blue}2] in [MATH: 4,{\color{blue}2}11] is [MATH: 100] times larger than the value of the digit [MATH: \color{red}2] in [MATH: 1{\color{red}2}.]

Content:

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Whenever you move a digit one space to the left in a place value chart, the value of the digit becomes ten times larger.

Content:
Let's use this idea to compare the size of the digit [MATH: 3] in the following two numbers:

Content:
[MATH: {\color{blue}3}8, \qquad 97{\color{red}3}]

Content:
We can compare the relative sizes of the digit [MATH: 3] for each number using a place value chart:

Content:
- First, we write down the place value chart for [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}8{:}]

| hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{lightgray}{0}] | [MATH: \color{blue}3] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}{8}] |
- Then, we write down the place value chart for [MATH: 97{\color{red}{3}}{:}]

| hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{lightgray}{9}] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}{7}] | [MATH: \color{red}3] |
- To compare the sizes of the two digits, we need to move one place to the left.

| hundreds | tens | ones |
| | [MATH: \color{blue}3] | [MATH: \color{red}3] |
| [IMG: /graphics/0257b37fd0a9e1ec6b1cbd4031a533d0] |

Content:
Since the digit [MATH: \color{blue}3] in [MATH: {\color{blue}3}8] is once space to the left of the digit [MATH: \color{red}3] in [MATH: 97{\color{red}3},] we can make the following conclusion:

Content:
> The value of the digit [MATH: \color{blue}3] in [MATH: {\color{blue}3}8] is [MATH: 10] times larger than the value of the digit [MATH: \color{red}3] in [MATH: 97{\color{red}3}.]

Whenever you move a digit one space to the left in a place value chart, the value of the digit becomes ten times larger.

Let's start by writing down the place values for [MATH: 57.]

| hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{lightgray}{0}] | [MATH: \color{red}5] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}7] |

We need to find a number in which the digit [MATH: \color{blue}5] has a value that is [MATH: 10] times larger than that of tens. So, we move [MATH: 1] step left in the place value chart:

| hundreds | tens | ones |

Item 5 — Tutorial: Comparing Place Values by Moving Multiple Steps to the Left

Content:
Let's compare the value of the digit [MATH: 2] in the following two numbers:

Content:
[MATH: 4,{\color{blue}2}11, \qquad 1{\color{red}2}]

Content:
- First, we write down the place value chart for [MATH: 4,{\color{blue}2}11{:}]

| thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{lightgray}4] | [MATH: \color{blue}2] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}1] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}1] |
- Then, we write down the place value chart for [MATH: 1{\color{red}2}{:}]

| thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{lightgray}{0}] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}{0}] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}1] | [MATH: \color{red}2] |
- To compare the sizes of the two digits, we need to move two places to the left:

| thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| | [MATH: \color{blue}2] | | [MATH: \color{red}2] |
| [IMG: /graphics/fca337b2cbbe679601303cc24abce6f0] |

Content:
Now, note the following:

Content:
- Whenever you move a digit one space to the left, the value of the digit becomes [MATH: 10] times larger.
- So, whenever you move a digit two spaces to the left, the value of the digit becomes [MATH: 10\times 10 = 100] times larger!

Content:
Therefore, we can make the following conclusion:

Content:
> The value of the digit [MATH: \color{blue}2] in [MATH: 4,{\color{blue}2}11] is [MATH: 100] times larger than the value of the digit [MATH: \color{red}2] in [MATH: 1{\color{red}2}.]

Content:
